items.answer: In one line: drive the ambulance safely to the right place and transport patients smoothly to the hospital. Work includes dispatch response, route selection, patient-moving assistance, smooth driving, vehicle maintenance, records, and handoffs.
items.question: What do ambulance drivers do?

rows.value: Ambulance, injured or ill patients, and transport routes

rows.label: Where Experience Matters Most
rows.value: Route judgment and smooth driving under lights and sirens

items.answer: BLS projects -1% employment growth from 2024–2034 (BLS OOH, 2026). Growing emergency and transport needs support roles. Intelligent dispatch improves routes without replacing driving. Drivers with emergency care skills are more competitive and can advance toward responder or dispatch management roles.
items.question: What is the job outlook for ambulance drivers?

items.answer: The U.S. median annual wage is about $34,330 (BLS OOH, 2026). Chinese mainland pay data is unofficial, not real-time, and refreshed quarterly (source, 2026-08). Compensation usually combines base pay and attendance allowances. Emergency centers offer relative stability, while commercial transport pays by trip or mileage.
items.question: How much do ambulance drivers earn?

page.definition_block: Ambulance Drivers And Attendants, Except Emergency Medical Technicians drive ambulances for emergency and medical transport, help injured and ill people enter, exit, and move, and provide basic care en route. They support transportation in prehospital emergency systems while working closely with EMTs.

rows.label: Work Environment
rows.value: Ambulance cab and patient compartment with changing environments, rotating shifts, and high pressure

rows.label: Education Requirement
rows.value: B/A class driver's license and first aid training, with no firm higher-education threshold

rows.label: Key Skills
rows.value: Driving, route planning, patient-moving assistance, basic care, and adaptability

rows.label: Core Activities
rows.value: Drive, move patients, provide basic care, maintain, and record

rows.label: Entry Requirement
rows.value: Low: licensed training is sufficient; advancement into emergency care requires additional credentials

responsibilities_block: Drive ambulances under dispatch instructions and select the best route for rapid arrival.
Help emergency personnel move injured and ill people and load and unload stretchers and equipment.
Drive smoothly during transport and support care in the patient compartment.
Keep vehicles clean, fueled, and fully stocked with emergency equipment.
Record trip and transport information and hand over vehicles and documents.
Support patient information handoffs with emergency personnel and hospitals.
page.work_context_block: When the alarm sounds, activate the siren and depart. Drive quickly but smoothly through chaotic traffic while emergency personnel work without distraction in the patient compartment. At the hospital, help move the patient into the emergency department. After handoff, clean and refuel the vehicle and return equipment to place. Then wait for the next alarm. Driving hundreds of miles in a day is common.

responsibilities_block: Load parts into baskets or racks and place them in cleaning or pickling equipment according to process requirements.
Set cleaning temperature, time, bath concentration, and other process parameters.
Monitor equipment and bath conditions, replenish chemicals, and adjust parameters promptly.
Remove processed parts, then rinse, neutralize, and dry them.
Inspect surface-treatment quality and rework or report defects.
Maintain equipment, record production data, and follow chemical safety procedures.
page.work_context_block: Operators move through a humid workshop wearing protective gloves and goggles. They load baskets, lower parts into tanks, monitor time, remove parts, and rinse them. Automated machines still require close attention because high temperatures, low liquid levels, and jammed parts demand immediate action. The job involves extensive walking and constant chemical odors.

page.work_context_block: A night shift can bring consecutive traffic injuries, heart attacks, and poisonings. Triage the most critical patient into the resuscitation room, then perform chest procedures and intubation without delay. After stabilization, contact specialty teams and update the family. Before dawn, guide residents through procedures and finish resuscitation records.

items.question: How much do Mail Clerks And Mail Machine Operators, Except Postal Service earn?

page.definition_block: Mail Clerks And Mail Machine Operators, Except Postal Service process correspondence and parcels in corporate, school, and institutional mailrooms, operate postage and sorting equipment, record tracking data, and coordinate carriers, serving as internal logistics hubs.

rows.label: Education Requirement
rows.value: High school diploma or technical secondary school + training

rows.label: Key Skills
rows.value: Sorting, postage machines, systems, reconciliation, and attention to detail

rows.label: Core Activities
rows.value: Receive, dispatch, operate, record, and verify

responsibilities_block: Sort inbound and outbound items.
Operate postage meters for charging and marking.
Enter items into systems and generate labels and tracking.
Clear paper jams and handle exception items.
Reconcile accounts and manage supplies.
Coordinate carrier pickups and deliveries.
page.work_context_block: Begin by receiving inbound mail and sorting it by department. In the morning, run outbound invoices through the postage meter, scan them, and generate labels. Clear jams as needed. Later, reconcile weekly postage bills, contact carriers for pickups, register exceptions, clean the mailroom, and prepare supplies for the next day.

page.definition_block: Physicists study the fundamental laws of matter and energy, use mathematical modeling and experimental validation, propose and test theories about nature, and advance the boundaries of scientific knowledge and technology.

rows.label: Work Environment
rows.value: Universities / national laboratories / corporate research and development

responsibilities_block: Develop research hypotheses and mathematical models.
Design experiments and calibrate and operate instruments.
Collect data and control errors and background noise.
Use simulations and fitting to validate results.
Write papers and undergo peer review.
Mentor students and manage projects and funding.
page.work_context_block: In the morning, derive formulas or review simulations completed overnight. At midday, discuss anomalous data in a group meeting and decide whether to repeat the work or publish. In the afternoon, adjust optical paths or cryogenic systems in the laboratory. In the evening, read literature for breakthroughs, and late at night respond to peer-review comments and email.
